expected.rationale: Power is explicitly irrelevant at 106 yards. PGA Tour's own coverage frames the challenge as hitting a small, well-bunkered target precisely (STRAIGHT) while improvising a soft, wind-adjusted trajectory (TOUCH, using that exact word) — no source supports a single archetype over the other.
sources: PGA Tour, 'Pebble Beach's short but tall task'
PGA Tour, 'AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am 2025 Course Stats'
Golf Monthly, '5 Facts About Pebble Beach's Famous Par-3 7th Hole'

approximations: scoring average is from the 2025 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am (a calm-conditions, non-major week); the hole's real scoring is famously wind-driven and can range far higher (77.27 field average in the storm-hit final round of the 1992 U.S. Open), so the plausibility check here has less signal than it would for a major-championship hole
ocean/cliff surrounds on three sides approximated as an OB boundary plus rough beyond, not literal water
green scaled to 80% of the green-small primitive to approximate the hole's unusually small target
